newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: CABINET LIKELY TO REJECT HEROIN TRIAL
Federal Cabinet appears set to reject a heroin trial for the ACT when it considers the matter in Melbourne tomorrow.
Health Minister Michael Wooldridge is expected to report to Cabinet on the ACT's proposal for an alternative treatment for 40 addicts.
The trial was supported last month at a meeting of State and Commonwealth Health ministers chaired by Dr Wooldridge.
But last week Prime Minister John Howard expressed his reservations, saying he was profoundly sceptical about the trial.
Cabinet Ministers have indicated that the issue is unlikely to survive past tomorrow's Cabinet meeting.
LIBERAL PARTY PROBES BROTHEL CLAIM
The Queensland branch of the Liberal Party is investigating claims it was a Liberal Federal MP who was questioned by police after a Brisbane brothel raid .
State director Greg Goebel said he would speak to police today to confirm the identity of the person involved.
He said he was yet to speak to the politician in question.
Mr Goebel said if police confirmed they did question a Liberal MP, the party would have to look at the matter closely.
"This is not the sort of thing the Liberal Party condones at all," he said.
"We have a number of hard-working Liberal MPs out there in the community, and we want to make sure that they're in the clear and getting on with the job."
REMISSION BUT NO FREEDOM FOR EAST TIMOR RESISTANCE LEADER
The Indonesian Government has granted a three-month sentence remission to jailed East Timorese resistance leader Xanana Gusmao and said he might be offered further reductions of his 20-year sentence.
Indonesian Justice Minister Utorgo Ousman has stressed the move has nothing to do with a recent appeal for clemency for Mr Gusmao from South African President Nelson Mandela.
Mr Ousman said Mr Gusmao could be free before the completion of his 20-year jail term if he kept up his good conduct.
He said he expected that term to end after the year 2000.
There had been intense speculation this past week that President Suharto might choose the 52nd anniversary of Indonesia's independence to grant Mr Mandela's request for Mr Gusmao's release.
UNION PRAISES TOYOTA PRODUCTION BOOST, BUT NOT PM
Toyota's decision to increase production in Australia has come in spite of the Federal Government, not because of it, according to the Manufacturing Workers Union.
National secretary Doug Cameron said the news was proof that tariffs protected and created jobs.
But he said he would not be passing on any thanks to Prime Minister John Howard for the tariff freeze.
"I've never felt a great warmth towards the Prime Minister and his Industrial Relations policies," Mr Cameron said.
"The Liberal conservative government was forced to change their position on tariffs.
"They were wrong when they started out, the productivity commission was wrong, and the community and union campaign forced them to change their position.
"So it was good news for the Australian community that they did change their position."
MP BLASTS BLAN TO BOYCOTT AIRPORTS
Airline pilots' threat to boycott Launceston and Hobart airports have been labelled irresponsible by a Tasmanian Federal Member of Parliament.
Members of the Australian and International Pilots Association said they had safety concerns about a new airspace management plan being considered by the Civil Aviation Safety Authority.
Warwick Smith, the Federal member for Bass, said the pilots' threat was premature because the plan was still in draft form and open to comment.
Mr Smith said he did not believe the plan would pose safety problems for regional airports.
INDEPENDENT WANTS REFERENDUM ON RADICAL' HEROIN TRIAL
Australian Capital Territory Independent politican Paul Osborne will seek a referendum on Canberra's proposed heroin trial.
Mr Osborne said he was incensed Chief Minister Kate Carnell had managed to gain the support of a majority of Australia's Health Ministers for what he called a "radical social experiment".
In his toughest attack yet on the Government he has supported for two-and-a-half years, Mr Osborne said the Chief Minister had acted without a mandate to inflict her proposal on Canberra.
"For too long we've been the social experiment capital of Australia," he said.
"And I believe the people out there need to have a say and decide whether this is the path they want to tread."
CHAMBER OF COMMERCE WELCOMES PM'S MOVE ON TAX REFORM
The Chamber of Commerce and Industry has welcomed Prime Minister John Howard's moves on tax reform and industry policy, predicting business confidence will take off soon.
The Chamber said it was pleased Mr Howard had responded to business concern that the Government was failing to create a sense of direction.
It said business needed a sense of purpose to make investment decisions and an end to the sense of drift it had seen from the Government.

Executive director Mark Paterson said business was comforted by Mr Howard kick-starting the tax reform debate and his willingness to consider strategic intervention for industry through expenditure or tax concessions.
Mr Paterson said he hoped the Government would act on industry policy within weeks, paving the way for greater business confidence and employment.
"It's not going to make dramatic changes in relation to the unemployment situation overnight," he said.
"That clearly will take time to work through."
